title: 3rd Stopping Place 4th Truth The Seal Of Unity In The Manifestation Of The Compassionate And The Provider

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage about one apple?
questions.answer: Even one apple shows that its true Giver must be the Creator Who controls the whole world.

questions.question: Which big things are mentioned as being under Allah’s control in order for fruit to reach people?
questions.answer: The seasons, the day and night cycle, and the turning of the earth are mentioned.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect a single apple to the whole earth?
questions.answer: Because the apple depends on a huge system in the world, not just on itself alone.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the earth is like a garden for the apple?
questions.answer: It means the earth is the wide place where the apple and other living things are grown and cared for.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the universe to when speaking about where the apple is produced?
questions.answer: It compares the universe to a tree and to a book.

questions.question: How do spring and summer help in the example?
questions.answer: They are shown as the times when the fruit grows and becomes ready.

questions.question: What idea is taught by saying the same mark is found on all fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: It teaches that they all come from the same Maker.

questions.question: Who is described as the true Owner and Maker of the apple?
questions.answer: The majestic and beautiful Creator of all living things and of the whole world.

questions.question: What does it mean that every fruit is a “seal of unity”?
questions.answer: Each fruit points to one Creator and is a sign that creation comes from Him alone.

questions.question: How does the last sentence strengthen the message of Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It says that every fruit gives its own witness, so the signs of unity are many and repeated.

questions.question: According to the passage, can an apple be explained by a small, separate cause only?
questions.answer: No. It needs the work of the One Who runs the whole universe.

questions.question: Why are the changing seasons important in the argument?
questions.answer: They help bring different foods at the right times, showing wise planning.

questions.question: What picture is given of the earth when people receive fruits from it?
questions.answer: The earth is pictured like a ship carrying goods to needy guests.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be seen on the apple itself?
questions.answer: It says there are signs of wise design, mercy, and neediness on it.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention other apples, fruits, plants, and animals too?
questions.answer: To show that the same kind of sign appears on all of them, so they have one Maker.

questions.question: If one Being made the apple, what else must also belong to Him according to the passage?
questions.answer: The earth, the seasons, the larger world, and the creatures connected with the apple must also belong to Him.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage give between the apple and other creatures in the world?
questions.answer: It says they are like its companions and related fellow-creatures.

questions.question: What is meant by calling fruit a “seal”?
questions.answer: It means fruit is like a mark of ownership that points to its true Maker.

questions.question: What is the main lesson a student should take from the whole passage?
questions.answer: Small blessings like fruit should lead us to recognize Allah’s power, wisdom, mercy, and oneness.

questions.question: What everyday object is used in the passage to teach a big truth?
questions.answer: An apple is used.

questions.question: What big truth does the apple teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah alone is the Maker and Provider.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about night and day turning one after another?
questions.answer: To show that even the giving of fruit depends on the order of the whole world.

questions.question: How is the earth described in a way that sounds like travel and delivery?
questions.answer: It is described like a loaded ship bringing food to those who need it.

questions.question: What does this image of a ship help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see that food reaches people through a planned and controlled system.

questions.question: What qualities are connected to the apple in the passage?
questions.answer: Wisdom, mercy, and a sign of dependence are connected to it.

questions.question: How does the passage move from one apple to all creation?
questions.answer: It says the same signs found on one apple are also found on all similar created things.

questions.question: Why is the Maker of the apple also said to be the Maker of the cosmos?
questions.answer: Because the apple depends on the larger world and carries the same signs found throughout creation.

questions.question: What do the comparisons to a tree, garden, factory, and workshop show?
questions.answer: They show that the apple’s growth is part of a complete, organized process.

questions.question: In the final idea of the passage, what does every fruit announce?
questions.answer: Every fruit announces Allah’s unity and points back to Him.

questions.question: What is being argued through the example of a single fruit?
questions.answer: The passage argues that even one fruit proves the existence of one all-powerful Creator.

questions.question: Why is the turning of the earth mentioned?
questions.answer: Because bringing fruits to people requires control over the world itself.

questions.question: What does the phrase about people waiting for fruits suggest about human beings?
questions.answer: It suggests that people need provision and depend on Allah for it.

questions.question: What can we infer from the apple having signs of mercy on it?
questions.answer: We can infer that its giving is not random but comes from a caring Creator.

questions.question: What can we infer from the apple having signs of wisdom on it?
questions.answer: We can infer that it was made with purpose and order.

questions.question: Why does the passage include animals along with plants and fruits?
questions.answer: To show that the same divine signature appears across all living things.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the apple to the seasons?
questions.answer: It says the seasons are part of the process by which the apple is developed and brought forth.

questions.question: What does the image of the universe as a book suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that creation is meaningful and can be read as signs pointing to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by speaking about the number of fruits?
questions.answer: To show that the proofs of Allah’s oneness are countless and repeated again and again.

questions.question: In simple words, why can’t one apple be separated from the rest of creation?
questions.answer: Because it depends on the earth, time, weather, and many other things in the world.

questions.question: What does the passage say is needed for fruit to be brought within people’s reach?
questions.answer: The world must be run in an ordered way through changing times and movements.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the same mark being on many different living things?
questions.answer: The lesson is that they come from one Lord, not from many separate makers.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the earth in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: It describes the earth as the apple’s garden.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the cosmos in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: It describes the cosmos as a great tree and also as something like a place where the apple is produced.

questions.question: What role do spring and summer play in the example?
questions.answer: They are the times in which the apple grows and ripens.

questions.question: Why is the apple called a sign of unity rather than just a piece of food?
questions.answer: Because it points beyond itself to Allah, its one Creator.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about looking at ordinary blessings?
questions.answer: It teaches that ordinary blessings should make us think about Allah’s greatness and mercy.

questions.question: If every fruit is a sign, what should a believer notice when seeing many fruits?
questions.answer: A believer should notice many reminders of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the strongest conclusion of the passage?
questions.answer: The Creator of one fruit is the Creator of the whole universe.

questions.question: What small thing is used to prove a very large idea in the passage?
questions.answer: A single apple is used to prove a very large idea.

questions.question: What is that large idea?
questions.answer: Allah alone is the Maker of the world and the Giver of provision.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the movement of day, night, and the earth?
questions.answer: To show that even one fruit depends on the rule of the whole creation.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about where fruits come from in the deepest sense?
questions.answer: It teaches that fruits truly come from Allah, not just from nearby visible causes.

questions.question: What signs on the apple are pointed out in the passage?
questions.answer: Signs of wisdom, mercy, and complete dependence are pointed out.

questions.question: Why is it important that the same signs are found on many created things?
questions.answer: It is important because it shows one plan and one Maker behind them all.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying other creatures are like the apple’s brothers?
questions.answer: It means they belong to the same creation and come from the same Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage use different pictures like garden and workshop?
questions.answer: It uses them to help us imagine the stages and places involved in the fruit’s growth.

questions.question: What does every fruit make known, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Every fruit makes known the One Who made the earth and the universe.

questions.question: How would this passage help a Muslim student grow in iman?
questions.answer: It helps the student see Allah’s oneness and care through simple blessings they can observe every day.
